title: Richard E. Olson, et al. v. Heritage Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC held the case administratively out of order and not properly before it on two independent grounds: the complaint was not timely filed with the General Assembly, and the Presbytery's response to a non-judicial reference seeking advice under BCO 41-3 is not a matter for complaint. The SJC distinguished judicial references, which go to the SJC, from non-judicial references, which go to the Committee on Constitutional Business, and noted that complainants could submit their questions there. The proposed disposition was confirmed 23-0 on March 18, 1992.
first_summary: The SJC dismissed Olson et al.'s complaint against Heritage Presbytery's adoption of a report on requiring officer abstinence from alcohol. The complaint was untimely filed with the General Assembly, and the Presbytery's response to a non-judicial reference was not complainable. The SJC affirmed 23-0.
summary: Heritage Presbytery adopted a committee report answering a session's reference on whether a session may require officers to abstain from beverage alcohol. Olson and others complained. The SJC held the complaint administratively out of order because it was not timely filed with the General Assembly, and independently ruled that a court's response to a non-judicial reference seeking advice under BCO 41-3 is not complainable. Complainants may submit their questions to the Committee on Constitutional Business. Confirmed 23-0.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Lines 1–5 identify Judicial Case No. 92-3, Standing Judicial Commission, 20th Assembly (1992), disposition administratively out of order. Lines 58–64 record that the proposed disposition was confirmed by the SJC 23-0 on March 18, 1992.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 18–34 describe the session's reference asking whether a session may require total abstinence from beverage alcohol for church officers, the Presbytery's adoption of committee recommendations on September 14, 1991, Olson et al.'s complaint, the Presbytery's denial on November 9, 1991, and the complainants' filing with the General Assembly on December 12, 1991.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 44–56 state the SJC's holding that the case was administratively out of order because it was not timely filed with the General Assembly, and separately that the response of a court to a non-judicial reference seeking advice under BCO 41-3 is not complainable. The SJC noted that judicial references go to the SJC and non-judicial references to the Committee on Constitutional Business. Lines 58–60 confirm the vote.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC did not reach the merits of the scriptural or constitutional abstinence questions. Line 69 references SJC Docket 92-4, Conrad et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery, and is not part of the 1992-03 disposition.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No incorporated decision supplies a result for 1992-03. The line 69 cross-reference to SJC Docket 92-4 is an adjacent/separate matter and was not treated as an adopted reason or disposition in this case.
